name: Self-reversing screw
summary: A screw cut with a right-hand and a left-hand groove joined at the ends drives a shoe to and fro at constant speed while it turns one way.

ratio.typical: one lead per turn (48 mm by default); stroke = lead x (turns per traverse - turn-round), 120 mm over 3 turns

topology.notes: ground, screw (revolute in its pillow blocks), carriage (prismatic on its guide), shoe (revolute pivot in the carriage); the shoe in the groove is a form-closed cam contact; counted mobility 2, because the shoe's swivel on its pivot is set by the groove's walls, which the count does not see

explain.motion: The screw carries a right-hand and a left-hand groove of the same lead, joined at both ends into one endless track that crosses itself twice on every turn. A shoe rides the groove on a pivot in the carriage. Turning the screw one way at a steady speed carries the shoe along at a steady 48 mm per turn. Near each end the groove bends round within 1 turn of the screw: the shoe slows, stops, swivels across into the other groove and comes back, so the carriage runs 120 mm there and back every 6 turns with the screw never changing direction.
explain.forces: The groove's wall pushes on the side of the shoe, and the push along the screw is the turning effort over the lead, less friction. At the pitch radius the grooves lean 28.6° from the circumference, so the shoe swivels through 57.2° at each turn-round. Where the grooves cross, the shoe loses its walls in the middle and is carried by its two ends, which is why it must be longer than a crossing.
explain.benefits: Turns steady one-way rotation into a steady to-and-fro with no reversing gear, clutch or change of direction, and the reversal points are cut into the screw, so they never drift.
explain.limits: The stroke and the reversal points are fixed when the screw is cut. The sharp points where the grooves cross and the long shoe wear fastest, and a worn shoe can turn into the wrong groove and reverse early; heavy loads wear the shoe quickly.

build.ground: base with the screw's two pillow blocks and a straight guide for the carriage along the screw
build.defining_relations: Both grooves have the lead p = 48 mm; at the pitch radius rp = 14 mm the lead angle is atan(p / (2 pi rp)) = 28.6°. Over each traverse of N = 3 turns the shoe moves by the trapezoidal law: steady at one lead per turn, with a parabolic turn-round of tr = 0.5 turn at each end (blend tr / N = 1/6), so the stroke is h = p (N - tr) = 120 mm and the track repeats after 2N = 6 turns. The shoe lies along the groove: its swivel is the change of atan(s' / rp), plus or minus 28.6° in the steady runs. Groove 7 mm wide and 4 mm deep; at the lead angle a crossing is 7 / sin(57.2°) = 8.3 mm long along the groove, bridged by a shoe 18 mm long.
build.notes: Screw axis horizontal, the shoe on the near side, seen in front elevation where the grooves cross in a diamond pattern. The track is cut by Manifold in pieces along the law, the root turned back as one core. The shoe's blade is an ellipse in plan, its underside cut round the screw's axis; it swivels on a pivot bolt in the carriage's upright.

groove.centreline: x = s(theta) at the pitch radius, theta over 6 turns: right hand out, left hand back
groove.make: boolean: the track cut in pieces of the groove's section along the law, the root turned back as one core

joints.note: at is the shoe's centre at the pitch radius Rp (mid-depth of the groove); the track's centre line runs along the axis by the law over 2N turns, so it crosses itself

params.note: turns of the screw per traverse
turn-round at each end, turns of the screw

review.note: New record, reviewed against its kinematics before the build (#255). Six phases of the solved cycle (every 60 degrees of the cycle, one turn of the screw): the shoe at mid-stroke on a crossing, 48 mm further, at the far end turning round (swivel through 0 to -57.2), and back the same way; the shoe's travel against the screw's turn is an exact triangle wave with rounded tips, 24 mm per half turn in the steady runs. Decided: 3 turns per traverse and a turn-round of half a turn either side of each end, so the cycle is 6 turns, the shoe runs steady for 2 of every 3 turns and the turn-round is a sixth of the cycle, long enough to watch with no time map; lead 48 on a 32 mm screw, a lead angle of 28.6 degrees at the 14 mm pitch radius, so a crossing is 8.3 mm long and an 18 mm shoe bridges it with 4.8 mm in the groove at each end; the reference at mid-stroke, where both grooves cross under the shoe, so the opening drawing shows the shoe bridging a crossing. Default view FRONT, the screw's near side where the grooves cross in diamonds and the shoe lies along its groove at true size. One tick per screw turn on the shoe's trace, a fixed one-lead dimension above it and the stroke dimension between the posed ends, so a turn reads as one lead; plot of the shoe's position against the screw's turn (the triangle wave over 6 turns); a detail view at the crossing under the shoe at the reference. The carriage is drawn see-through on purpose (teaching.seeThrough): its upright stands in front of the shoe in FRONT. Controls: the screw's turn only; the lead, turns and turn-round are built into the screw, so they are not offered.

claims.text: carries the shoe along at a steady 48 mm per turn
the carriage runs 120 mm there and back
every 6 turns: out in 3 turns (half the cycle)
bends round within 1 turn of the screw (a sixth of the cycle below full speed at each end)

name: Wobble box
summary: A turning shaft with an inclined journal nods a trunnioned ring, which rocks an output shaft at right angles to and fro through the journal's angle.

ratio.typical: output swing ±α, the journal's angle to the shaft (±15° here); arm stroke 2 L sin α

topology.notes: ground, input shaft with its inclined journal, the trunnion ring, the output shaft with its yoke; a spherical four-bar, the four revolute axes (input shaft, journal, trunnions, output shaft) meeting at one centre. The kin block keeps the journal sleeve pinned on the input and the arm keyed on the output as bodies of their own (posed with them), so the joint count does not give the mobility: Kutzbach counts 5, which ignores the concurrent axes and counts the sleeve's spin; the true mobility is 1, solved in closed form by the spherical-four-bar block. The loop is overconstrained in the count, as a universal joint is.

explain.motion: The input shaft carries a journal set at a small angle α to its axis, and a ring turns on the journal in bearings. Trunnion pins on the ring, square to the journal, sit in a yoke on an output shaft that stands square to the input. All four axes meet at one centre, so the ring cannot turn with the shaft: it nods, and the yoke rocks the output to and fro through exactly ±α while the input turns on. The swing follows ψ = atan(tan α sin θ), close to a sine, and an arm on the output turns it into a stroke of 2 L sin α.
explain.forces: The input torque reaches the output as a pair of forces on the trunnions, carried by the ring's bearings on the journal. The output moves fastest, at tan α times the input speed, as it passes mid-swing, and its reaction then twists the journal hardest; at the ends of the swing it stands still and a load on the arm cannot turn the input.
explain.benefits: It turns a fast shaft into a strong, smooth, nearly sinusoidal rocking in a compact sealed unit, with only turning bearings and no sliding guides.
explain.limits: The swing is fixed by the journal's angle, so changing the stroke means a new journal. The axes must meet at one point: a machining or shimming error loads the bearings and wears them quickly, and the rocking mass shakes the frame at high speed.

build.ground: base plate with the input shaft's two pillow blocks and the output shaft's, the two axes square and meeting at the centre
build.defining_relations: spherical four-bar with input link α (journal to shaft), coupler 90° (journal to trunnions), output link 90° (trunnions to output shaft), ground 90° (input to output); output angle ψ = atan(tan α sin θ), θ from the pose where the journal leans in the plane of the two shafts (equivalently ψ = atan(tan α cos θ) counted from the pose square to it); amplitude exactly α; output speed ratio dψ/dθ = tan α cos θ / (1 + tan²α sin²θ), at most tan α; arm stroke 2 L sin α
build.notes: Input 360° continuous; the output rocks ±15° at α = 15° and a 60 mm arm sweeps a chord of 31.1 mm. Every axis must pass through the centre. The ring's bearings on the journal take the trunnion loads; the trunnions turn in needle cups in the yoke's arms. At θ = 0 the journal leans in the plane of the two shafts, the trunnions stand upright and the yoke and arm are at mid-swing.

bodies.note: the wobble hub's straight shank, keyed on the input shaft; the inclined journal is one piece with it
the wobble hub's inclined journal, turned at alpha to the shaft on a collar that runs back into the straight shank: one forging with it, bored for the shaft

joints.note: the ring on the inclined journal, on two bearings
the ring's trunnions in the yoke, square to the journal
output shaft, square to the input, through the same centre
the arm keyed on the output shaft

params.note: journal angle to the input shaft: the swing amplitude
arm length, output axis to the arm's tip (the arm's shape length)

opts.relation: psi = atan(tan(alpha) sin(theta)), the root through the reference pose

review.note: T2 before the build, from the solved kinematics: six phases at 60 degrees of input give swings of 0, -13.1, -13.1, 0, +13.1, +13.1 degrees, so the yoke and the arm visibly rock while the shaft turns; the solve matches psi = atan(tan(alpha) sin(theta)) to 2e-14 at 8, 15 and 25 degrees, amplitude exactly alpha, within 0.13 degrees of a pure sine at 15; the arm tip sweeps 31.1 mm; the output's speed ratio peaks at tan(alpha) at mid-swing; no dwell. Decided: the output shaft lies in plan square to the input, as the universal joint's does, so the two relatives read side by side; the reference pose is mid-swing (journal leaning in the plane of the two shafts, trunnions upright, yoke and arm upright), so the journal angle reads true in PLAN at the start; the journal angle is a control (5 to 25 degrees) with a ghost trace and plot ghosts at 8 and 25, because 'the swing is the journal's angle' is the lesson; the arm's tip is traced with equal-time ticks every 15 degrees (bunched at the ends of the stroke, near harmonic) and a rim point of the ring is traced to show its nod; construction: the four axis lines (input, journal, trunnion, output) and a circle at the common centre, the journal angle arc, the stroke dimension; default view ISOMETRIC, where all four axes and the nod read at once; section A-A through the input and journal axes at the start shows the inclined journal inside the ring on its bearings, the one part of the principle a housing hides; no use context in the drawing.

views.note: through the input axis and the journal axis at the start: the inclined journal inside the ring, on its two bearings
